parole.significato: industrial, concerning an industry or industry in general
parole.testo: Borrowed from French industriel, from Latin industria (“industry, zeal”).

From French interpolation, from Latin interpolātiō.

parole.significato: an introduction (act or process of introducing; something that presents or introduces)

Borrowed from French ironie, Latin īrōnīa.
Borrowed from French irrigation, from Latin irrigātiō.
Borrowed from French irriguer, from Latin irrigō.

parole.significato: cup (like a cup of coffee or tea)

From French cadavre, from Latin cadāver.

Borrowed from French caryatide, from Latin caryatides, from Ancient Greek Καρυάτιδες (Karuátides).
Borrowed from French caserne, ultimately from Latin quaternus.

Borrowed from French lancer, ultimately from Latin lancēre.
Borrowed from French langouste, from Latin locusta (“locust; lobster”).

parole.significato: a very simple toilet facility, usually just a pit or trench; a latrine
parole.testo: From French latrine (“latrine”), from Latin lātrīna (“bath; toilet”).
Borrowed from French lavabo, from Latin lavābō (“I will wash”), first-person singular future active indicative of lavō, lavāre (“wash, bathe”, verb).

parole.significato: linear (having the form of a line)

parole.significato: magic, sorcery (occult woo, black or white magic, etc.); hence supernatural occurrences or phenonomena
parole.testo: Borrowed from French magie, from Middle French magie, from Latin magīa, from Ancient Greek μαγεία (mageía).
From French marine, from Latin marinus, derived from mare (“sea”).
From French maritime, from Latin maritimus.
Borrowed from French martial, from Latin martiālis.

parole.significato: mechanical, related to mechanics and/or machinery
parole.testo: From French méchanique 'mechanical' and 'mechanics', from Latin mechanicus 'engineer' and 'resourceful, mechanical', ultimately from Ancient Greek (compare machine).
Borrowed from French membraneux, from Middle French membraneux, from Latin membrāneus.

Borrowed from French métaphore, from Latin metaphora, from Ancient Greek μεταφορά (metaphorá), from μεταφέρω (metaphérō, “to transfer, apply”), from μετά (metá, “with, across, after”) + φέρω (phérō, “to bear, carry”).
Borrowed from French mètre, from Latin metrum, from Ancient Greek μέτρον (métron). Doublet of metrum.

parole.significato: migration (moving to live in another place)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French migration, from Latin migrātiō. By surface analysis, migreren + -atie.

parole.significato: grand (sum of the value of 1,000 monetary units)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French mille (“thousand”), from Latin mīlle.

parole.significato: ministry (government department under the authority of a minister)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French ministère and influenced by Latin ministerium.

Borrowed from French mondial, from Latin mundiālis.

parole.significato: monolith (structure made from one stone or rock)

Borrowed from French narratif, from Middle French narratif, from Latin narrativus.

parole.significato: a female member of a Roman Catholic fraternity or lay organisation
